title: Coil-built nesting bowls set of three
subtitle: Three graduated air-dry clay bowls that stack inside each other for storage
excerpt: A nesting bowl set is three graduated coil-built bowls in air-dry clay that stack inside each other when not in use. The coil method builds the walls in rings that are then smoothed inside and out into a uniform curve. No kiln is needed. An intermediate maker building all three pieces in a single session will have a coordinated set that can be decorated identically or with a running motif across the three sizes.
sourceNotes: Coil building method derived from first principles. Graduated nesting form proportions referenced from V&A open-access collection (20th century studio ceramics). Air-dry clay properties from standard ceramics literature.

content.text: A nesting bowl set is three graduated
coil

-built bowls in air-dry clay, sized so each bowl sits neatly inside the one above it when stored. The three bowls measure approximately 8 cm, 12 cm, and 16 cm across at the rim. No kiln is needed. An intermediate maker building all three in one session will develop a rhythm for rolling coils and smoothing walls that produces a coordinated set.

materials.name: Clay slip (same clay body, thinned with water)
Acrylic paint or coloured slip for decoration (optional)
Matte acrylic varnish or PVA diluted 50/50 for sealing

tools.name: Banding wheel (makes turning the bowl easier)

content.text: Preparation

Set up three work boards so each bowl can sit undisturbed as the others are built. For nesting to work, the largest bowl's interior diameter must be at least 1.5 cm wider than the exterior diameter of the next bowl. Plan the three rim sizes: 16 cm, 12 cm, and 8 cm at the widest point. Wall thickness throughout will be 6-7 mm. Mark these dimensions on each work board with a pencil before starting. Prepare a generous batch of
score-and-slip
slip in a small lidded pot to keep it from drying out.
Building each bowl
The method is the same for all three bowls. Build the largest first, then the medium, then the small, so you have the largest form to check proportions against.

Roll a base circle from a flattened disc of clay, 6 mm thick. Cut to the correct diameter for each bowl: 10 cm, 7 cm, and 4.5 cm. These smaller bases will flare outward as the walls curve up. Place each base on a separate work board and allow to stiffen for 15 minutes before adding the first coil.

Roll the first coil for each bowl: a rope 6-7 mm in diameter. Roll on a smooth surface under both palms, working outward from the centre. A consistent thickness is more important than speed. Aim for a coil at least 40 cm long for the large bowl, 30 cm for the medium, and 20 cm for the small.

Score the top edge of the base and the underside of the first coil. Apply slip to both surfaces. Press the coil around the outer edge of the base, joining the two ends of the coil with a diagonal cut so the join is not a blunt butt-end. Press the join firmly and blend with a fingertip.

Blend the interior join between the base and the first coil thoroughly with a wooden rib, pressing the clay down into the corner. Work around the circumference twice. The interior join is structural: a poorly blended join will crack at this point on drying.

Add subsequent coils in the same way, scoring and slipping each join, staggering the start point of each coil by a quarter-turn so the joins do not stack vertically. As the walls grow, angle each successive coil slightly outward to build the bowl's flare. For a bowl with a 16 cm rim from a 10 cm base, each coil shifts outward by about 3-4 mm across the full diameter per ring.

Smooth the interior of each bowl after every two coils using the wooden rib and a damp sponge. Blend the coil joins into a continuous curved wall, working upward from the base. Do not smooth the exterior until all coils are placed: the exterior texture can be refined last, or left to show the coil construction as a decorative feature.

Build the large bowl to a height of about 7 cm, the medium to 5 cm, and the small to 3.5 cm before finishing the rim. At the final coil, smooth the rim coil into the wall so the top edge is flush and even. Use a metal rib held at a shallow angle to scrape the rim level and remove any high points.

Check the exterior diameter at the rim of each bowl using calipers or a ruler. Compare the rim diameter of the medium bowl against the interior diameter of the large bowl: the medium's exterior should clear the large's interior by at least 1-1.5 cm. Adjust by gently pressing inward or outward on the rim before the clay stiffens.

Smooth the exterior of all three bowls with a metal rib. Work in long strokes from base to rim, keeping the rib nearly parallel to the wall surface. Finish with a damp sponge to remove any remaining rib marks.
Drying
Cover all three bowls loosely with plastic and dry slowly for the first 24 hours to reach
leather-hard

. At leather-hard, refine any uneven sections at the rim or base with a damp sponge. Do not nest the bowls together during drying: as air-dry clay shrinks slightly, stacked pieces can lock or crack each other. Separate bowls dry in two to four days at room temperature to
bone-dry
. Do not rush this stage with a fan heater or oven: too-fast drying cracks coil-built forms at the join lines.
Finishing

Paint and seal once fully bone-dry. A coordinated colour scheme across all three bowls ties the set together visually: use the same base colour on all three, then vary the interior colour or add a painted band near the rim in a second colour. Seal all surfaces with two coats of diluted PVA or matte acrylic varnish. Allow each coat to dry fully before applying the next.
Care

These bowls are decorative. Air-dry clay is not waterproof even when sealed: prolonged water contact will soften the clay body. Use for dry items only: keys, jewellery, loose change. Wipe clean with a dry cloth. Stack the set for storage but do not stack other items on top of them.
Variations

Leave the exterior coil lines visible and seal without smoothing. The raised coil rings give the set a textural, studio-craft look. Paint a contrasting colour wash into the recessed join lines between coils to emphasise the structure.
Add a scallop rim to the largest bowl. While the clay is still soft, pinch the top edge between thumb and forefinger at regular intervals. Space the indentations evenly all the way round.
Extend the set to four or five graduated bowls. Keep the diameter steps consistent (4 cm per size increment) and the height-to-diameter ratio the same across all pieces for a harmonious stack.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Crack appears along the coil join lines on drying
items.cause: The coil joins were not blended thoroughly on the interior, leaving a weak bond that opens as the clay shrinks
items.fix: At leather-hard, dampen the crack with a wet finger, apply fresh slip, and press closed with a wooden rib. For cracks that appear at bone-dry, mix a paste of clay dust and PVA and fill the crack before sealing

items.problem: Walls are uneven in thickness, thinner in some areas
items.cause: Coils were rolled to an inconsistent diameter and thinner sections built up fewer layers of clay
items.fix: At leather-hard, press small patches of clay onto the thin areas, blend with a rib, and smooth. Use guide sticks of consistent thickness when rolling future coils

items.problem: Bowls do not nest: the medium sits on the rim of the large rather than inside it
items.cause: The rim of the medium bowl is wider than the interior opening of the large bowl
items.fix: At leather-hard, gently press the rim of the medium bowl inward with both hands to reduce its diameter. Work in small increments all around the rim. If already bone-dry, the fit cannot be corrected without rebuilding

items.problem: Base warps upward at the centre during drying
items.cause: The base slab was dried on a non-absorbent surface, and the underside dried slower than the top
items.fix: At leather-hard, press the bowl gently onto a flat plaster bat or dry wooden board and leave overnight. If the base is already bone-dry and warped, fill the warp with a small clay pad bonded with PVA to level the base
